simple.meaning: אָמוֹץ (ʼÂmôwts) appears 13 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, beginning at 2 Kings 19:2. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, priesthood, prophetic witness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָמוֹץ (H531) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows אָמוֹץ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: אָמוֹץ (ʼÂmôwts) / H531 is tracked through 2 Kings 19:2, 2 Kings 19:20, 2 Kings 20:1, 2 Chronicles 26:22. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.

timeline.evidenceText: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says ‘You have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria, and I have heard you.
In those days Hezekiah was sick and dying. Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him, and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Set your house in order; for you will die, and not live.’ ”
Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote.
Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, prayed because of this, and cried to heaven.
Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his good deeds, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.
at that time Yahweh spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, “Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.” He did so, walking naked and barefoot.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Yahweh, the God of Israel says, ‘Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
In those days Hezekiah was sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.’ ”
